description: Issue #85: deterministic golden vectors for AuditLogChainWriter and AuditMerkleRoot. Pins the canonical hash form from docs/ops/audit-retention.md §2 and the Bitcoin-style duplicate-last-on-odd Merkle convention. Four chained rows for tenant=dev, strategy=copytrade-v1.

rows.note: Chain head: prior_row_hash is NULL → writer substitutes 32 zero bytes. actor is JSON null → serialized as len=0. Simple subject.

Chains from row 0. actor is empty string "" — MUST hash identically to row 0's NULL actor under the NULL≡empty rule. Subject has nested object with keys in non-sorted insertion order; JCS must re-sort to {a,b}.
Chains from row 1. Non-trivial subject with mixed insertion order, nested object, and an array. Tests RFC 8785 JCS key ordering (UTF-16 code-unit).
Chains from row 2. Operator-actor event. Simple subject. Forces the test corpus to cover four chain links (issue requirement: >= 4 deterministic rows).

merkle_root_3_leaves.note: Bitcoin-style duplicate-last-on-odd Merkle root over the first 3 rows' row_hash values. The 3-leaf size forces the odd-node rule to fire: at level 0, pair(row0,row1)+pair(row2,row2). At level 1, pair(L,R). Pins the convention named in docs/ops/audit-retention.md §2.

merkle_root_4_leaves.note: Even-leaf Merkle root over all 4 rows (cross-check; not load-bearing for the odd-node convention but useful as a parity test against any third-party verifier).
